To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the elastic tissue of the human skin and its arteries is severely degenerated in response to prolonged actinic radiation.

actinic granulomas and temporal arteritis are autoimmune diseases of the elastic tissue of the human skin and of the internal elastic lamina, respectively, that develop because of the degenerative effects of prolonged exposure to ultraviolet radiation.

actinically damaged, "elastotic" elastic tissue is the probable antigenic basis of granulomatous inflammation of skin and of temporal arteries and that the latter is an accelerated form of atherosclerosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the actinic degeneration of elastic tissues and the granulomatous reactions that may develop in relation to such actinic changes.
the pathologic changes that occur in elastic tissue in response to prolonged actinic radiation.
the actinic origin, pathogenesis, and clinical significance of actinic granularomas and temporal arteritis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
actinically degenerated elastic tissue is a likely antigenic basis for both actinic granulomatous lesions of the skin and temporal arteritis.
actinic elastosis and actinic granulomas of the skin are the same disease, and that the same disease is the basis of temporal and giant cell arteritis.

actinic granulomas of the skin, and temporal arteritis, are the result of a severe degeneration of the elastic tissue of the affected skin and arteries, and of a subsequent resorptive (autoimmune) reaction to this degenerated tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
actinically induced degeneration of elastic tissue in the skin and arteries may be a significant factor in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis and arteriosclerosis.
the elastic tissue of skin and arteries is subject to severe, actinically induced degenerative change, which is a precursor for the formation of granulomas and giant cells in both tissues.
actinic radiation is a potent accelerator of the atherosclerotic process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
actinic degeneration of elastic tissue is a major cause of granulomatous inflammation of both the skin and arteries.
actinic granulomas and temporal arteritis may represent the same disease process, and that this disease may be a form of "accelerating" atherosclerosis.
actinic granulomas of the skin and temporal arteritis are likely to share a common etiology, namely, severe degenerative changes in elastic tissue.
